Creator Kickstarter · Live Call

You have to believe in the path

And keep walking it before you have any proof.

What today is about

The difference between the people who build it and the people who stop somewhere

It is one of the biggest splits we see in this group. It is also not the one most people expect.

It has nothing to do with

Not one of these is the thing

How smart you are The perfect niche Being amazing at Instagram The perfect business strategy

It is believing in the path that you are on.

Choose a path, and believe in it enough to keep walking

Even when you do not have immediate proof that it is working.

Inside Remote Goats

The path we have laid out looks like this

01

Create content

You show up on social media, consistently.

02

Attract the right people

That content pulls in the people you can actually help.

03

Build trust

They get to know you and believe you know your thing.

04

Move them to email

A lead magnet takes them onto a list you own.

05

Keep helping

You stay useful to them, week after week.

06

Monetize

In a way that fits the business and the life you want.

To be clear

That is not the only way to build a business

It is the way we set up the Creator Kickstarter. Some of you will build something else on the side, or change your mind about the course or the coaching. That is fine.

There is a lot you can build from an audience of people who know you, like you, and want what you have.

What you already have

The fundamentals work for any business

Create good content Attract the right people Communicate what you do Build trust Turn followers into an audience you own Solve a problem

You have learned every one of these in this program. None of them is tied to one business model.

Now the part you have to decide

What are you building toward?

What do you see as your monetization path?

The most dangerous place to stand

The beginning of five paths, committing to none of them

ThenYou start building a course→You see someone making money as a travel influencer
ThenMaybe I should do that instead→Somebody tells you paid newsletters are exploding
ThenMaybe I should start a Substack→You see someone running retreats
ThenWow, that looks amazing→Somebody says AI businesses are the future

You get the point.

Six months later.

You have been really busy. And you have not gotten anywhere.

The rule we would give you

Pick your path. Give it six months before you pivot.

Otherwise you keep jumping from idea to idea, and the jumping is what costs you the year.

Question for the group

Has anyone here lived this one?

01

Have you experienced it?

Where you were not doing nothing. You were actually doing a lot. But you kept changing direction.

02

What did you try?

Name the different things you started, and how far each one actually got.

03

What made you switch?

Was it a real signal from your audience, or was it someone else's result showing up in your feed?

Section two

First: pick what you are building toward

Probably the biggest thing we want everyone thinking about today.

You are already doing the work

Showing up, implementing, getting better

You are posting consistently. You are putting into practice what you have learned. You are getting comfortable and your skills are improving. Some of you are building your email lists too.

All of that is worth a lot. And at some point it has to be moving toward something.

What we mostly talk about here

Courses, coaching, community

Courses

We grew a personal brand, and off the back of it we have sold a number of courses.

Coaching and consulting

How we posted on social and email is why we sold out multiple cohorts of this program.

Community

The one you are sitting in right now.

We talk about these three because they are the three we have actually done. They do not have to be your path.

There are so many other ways

Any of these can be the thing you are building toward

Travel creator working with brands and tourism boards Group trips Planning trips for people Digital travel itineraries An influencer business with sponsors and media offers Retreats Drop shipping A business on YouTube A paid newsletter or Substack A book, and speaking on stages

And maybe your audience helps you land on something none of us have talked about in this program. Be open to that.

Why the skills matter more than the model

The same foundation sells any of them

A twenty nine dollar digital product. A three thousand dollar coaching program. A ten day group trip through Italy. A travel planning service. A membership. A book. Or something none of us have thought of yet.

So, to be clear

There is no one business you have to build here.

But we do think you need to start choosing a direction.

There is a big difference between

A thing you are doing

  • “I'm growing an Instagram account.”
vs

A thing you are building

  • “I'm building an audience of people I eventually want to take on group trips.”
  • “I'm building an audience of Christian moms, because eventually I want to create a paid community for them.”
  • “I'm creating travel content because I want this to become an influencer business, where brands and tourism boards pay me to travel.”

Same work. Completely different purpose.

Once you know what you are building toward

Even the questions get better

You stop asking

  • “What should I post this week?”
vs

And start asking

  • What kind of audience do I need for the business I ultimately want?
  • What problems do those people have?
  • What do they already spend money on?
  • What could I eventually offer them?
  • What skills am I still missing?
  • What is the next step between here and that business?

And this is where believing in the path becomes important.

Once you choose what you want to build, you have to believe there is a path from where you are now to that destination.

And if you are not sure there is

Go and look for the evidence

Find the person who is crushing it with retreats. Or with drop shipping. Or with whatever you are considering.

You are looking for proof that the path exists. Other people have already left the markers.

We really want you thinking

“What could all of this eventually become?”

Once you choose a direction that excites you, and you can see evidence that other people have made it work, you get to think: that is where I am going. What is my next step?

Question for the group

Forget the follower count for a minute

01

Forget next week

Not what you are posting on Tuesday, and not next month either. Zoom out as far as you possibly can.

02

If it goes really well

Over the next few years, what do you actually want this to become?

03

What would it let you do?

What would you love for your audience to eventually make possible? If you do not know yet, that is okay. That is the question to start answering.

Section three

We have had to do this over and over

Twice now, from scratch, with no promise either would work.

When we started Goats On The Road

Nobody guaranteed it would turn into a business

There was no one standing there saying “keep going for X months and then this exact thing will happen.”

So we did the only thing we could

We looked at what other people were doing

We sawPeople making money from blogs→So that was possible
We sawPeople traveling long term→So that was possible too
We sawPeople building audiences on social media→Evidence the path existed

If they could do it, the path was real. Then it became our job to walk it.

And then the long stretch

Where the work did not look anything like the result

Spend hours writing something Publish it Learn SEO Take the photos Build the website Try new things

And nothing dramatic happened. Not once.

Then all of those small actions compounded

We got to travel the world. We built a business that gave us freedom. We designed our lives around where we wanted to be, instead of where an employer told us to be.

Not every part of getting there was fun. The destination made those stretches worth pushing through.

Then we moved into coaching and online education

Different path. Same principle.

What carried over

  • How to create content
  • How to build an audience
  • How to communicate with people online
  • How to build trust
  • How to grow an email list
+

What we had to learn

  • How do you create an offer?
  • How do you sell coaching?
  • How do you launch something?
  • How do you build a community?
  • How do you package what you know so it gets somebody a result?

The skills did not become useless. They became the foundation of the next one.

And since then

We have changed things, made mistakes, and had offers that worked better than others

Periods where business felt easy. Periods where we had to completely rethink what we were doing.

But that is just business.

Section four

It gets easier once you decide

Something happens the moment you say: this is my path, I believe it works, I am doing this.

Say this is your path

Now the work gets a lot simpler

InstagramYou post where the right people are.
→
Lead magnetSomething they really want, in exchange for an email.
→
Email listAn audience you actually own.
→
The offerA digital product or a service.

Because now you know what to do.

Your job is not to learn seventeen other business models.

Your job is to get really good at those four things.

Which turns the whole business into

A short list of solvable problems

How do I make better content? How do I post every day without it taking all day? How do I attract the right person? How do I create a lead magnet they actually want? How do I build a relationship with my list? What problem can I solve? What could I sell? How do I make the offer better? How do I communicate its value?

Every one of those is solvable. And every day you can wake up and move one of them forward.

But you have to actually move it forward.

Section five

Relentless action

Once you believe in the path, you move toward the destination without letting up.

Let us be precise about this

What we do not mean

  • Burning yourself out
  • Working ten hour days
  • Destroying your health
  • Never taking a weekend off
vs

What we do mean

  • Being unbelievably consistent about moving toward the thing you said you want

One of those burns you out. The other one compounds.

Where we have to call ourselves out

You can say “I really want to build a business”

Then go and look at your calendar. Did this week reflect that?

The honest audit

Look at last week and answer these

Did you create? Did you sell? Did you talk to potential customers? Did you improve your offer? Did you publish the reel? Did you learn a skill you needed? Did you write the email? Did you finish the lead magnet? Did you do the uncomfortable thing?

Or did you spend the week getting lost in learning?

There is a massive difference between wanting the result

and organizing your life around actually producing it.

Section six

The other side is worth it

Because this is not meant to be an endless grind.

We talk a lot about discipline and doing hard things

But the whole reason we do this is that the other side can be that good

We know that one firsthand.

So think about this one properly

What is at the end of your path?

Quitting the job

Maybe that is the whole thing for you.

A summer in Europe

Taking your kids there for a whole summer instead of one rushed week.

Never asking again

Never having to ask a boss for vacation time.

Not checking price tags

Money not being the thing you think about every single day.

Monday morning

Waking up actually excited about what you are working on.

Or something else

It only has to matter to you.

See that place.

Because there will be moments between here and there where you are going to need a reason to continue.

If the destination matters enough, and you know the path can take you there

the lull becomes a lot less scary. It is just part of the journey.

Discussion · three questions to leave you with

Three questions

01

What path are you choosing?

It does not have to be the path in the curriculum. It has to be a path that you are happy with.

02

What evidence do you have that it works?

Can you find someone doing it? Someone who has taught other people to do it, and they are successful too? Are there a lot of people doing it? Every one of them is proof that it works.

03

Are your actions consistent with someone who believes they will get there?

And if not, do you know what those actions are? Can you commit to them not just for one week, but every week for the next year? Two years?

Once you believe the destination exists, your only real job is to keep walking.
